## ACT scores
Question:
What are the average scores for students taking the ACT?
Response:
The ACT (formerly the American College Testing Program) assessment program measures educational development and readiness to pursue college-level coursework in English, mathematics, natural science, and social studies. Student performance on the tests does not reflect innate ability and is influenced by a student's educational preparedness.
In 1995, some 38 percent of all high school graduates took the ACT.1 In 2023, some 37 percent of high school graduates were projected to take the ACT. The minimum score on the ACT is 1 and maximum score is 36.

## National Average ACT Score Over Time
In 2024, the national average composite score (19.4) was the lowest since 1990.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1), [[3]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-3)
*   The overall percentage of graduates who take the ACT appears to be dropping, with the figure down by 21 percentage points from 10 years ago (57% in 2014 vs. 36% in 2024).[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1), [[4]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-4)

*   The average ACT score has been decreasing as well. In 2012, the average composite score was 21.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1), [[4]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-4) In 2024, it was 19.[[4]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-4), [[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)

## National Average ACT Score Over Time
*   Roughly 1.4 million students, or 36% of the U.S. high school graduating class of 2024, took the ACT.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)

*   This is much lower than the 58% of high school graduates who took the test in 2016.[[5]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-5)

*   In contrast, 1.97 million high school graduatestook the SAT in 2024, which is an increase from 1.7 million in 2022.[[7]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-7)

The ACT and SAT have many of the same components. For example, they are both approximately three hours in length. Both tests also cover reading, English (or language on the SAT), and math.
The two tests also have some key differences.

## National Average ACT Score Over Time
*   While they are roughly the same length, the ACT has many more questions than the SAT (215 questions vs. 154).

*   For the ACT, the minimum score is 1 and the maximum, 36.

*   For the SAT, scores range from 400-1600, with 400 being the lowest you can score and 1600 being the highest.

*   The ACT also has an additional science section that the SAT doesn't have.

## National Average ACT Score Over Time
### Average ACT Scores by Gender
Based on the 2024 ACT report, women students outperformed men. Women earned an average composite score of 19.6, which is 0.2 points higher than men's average composite score of 19.[[4]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-4), [[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)
Seven percent of test-takers selected "another gender" or "prefer not to respond." This group had an average composite score of 18.8.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)
*   In 2024, men scored 0.7 points higher in math and 0.3 points higher in science than women.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)

*   In 2024, women scored 1.0 point higher in both English and reading than men.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)

*   Students who selected another gender and those who did not select any gender scored the lowest in every section, 0.9 points behind women in English, 1.2 points behind men in math, and 1.0 point behind men in science.[[1]](https://www.bestcolleges.com/research/average-act-score/#fn-1)

In recent years, more and more students have been taking the ACT than ever before. But what does this change in participation rate mean for the average ACT score?
As you'll learn in this article, while ACT scores have been fairly stable in the last few years, **there have been some dips and peaks in scores in the last 30 years.** Let's take a look at what's happening.
_Feature image: Erjwiki/Wikimedia_

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years

Let's look at some charts for average ACT scores over the past couple of decades. These will show us some trends in the ACT world that have led to recent changes in the test.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 1992-1996
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**1992-1993**875,603 20.3 20.1 21.2 20.8**20.7**  
**1994**891,714 20.3 20.2 21.2 20.9**20.8**  
**1995**945,369 20.3 20.2 21.3 21**20.8**  
**1996**924,663 20.3 20.2 21.3 21.1**20.9**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1970-1998_
In the 1992-1996 ACT scores, there was a general **increase** in Math, Reading, and Science scores.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 1997-2001
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**1997**959,301 20.3 20.6 21.3 21.1**21**  
**1998**995,039 20.4 20.8 21.4 21.1**21**  
**1999**1,019,053 20.5 20.7 21.4 21**21**  
**2000**1,065,138 20.5 20.7 21.4 21**21**  
**2001**1,069,772 20.5 20.7 21.3 21**21**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1970-2001_

In the 1997-2001 ACT scores, there was an increase in English and Math and a decline in Science and Reading. Also, in 1999, the ACT **broke the one million test-taker ceiling** for the first time.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2002-2005
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**2002**1,116,082 20.2 20.6 21.1 20.8**20.8**  
**2003**1,175,059 20.3 20.6 21.2 20.8**20.8**  
**2004**1,171,460 20.4 20.6 21.3 20.9**20.9**  
**2005**1,186,251 20.4 20.7 21.3 20.9**20.9**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1995-2010_
From 2002 to 2005, there was **a slight but steady rise** in all scores across the board.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2006-2011
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Writing****Composite**  
**2006**1,206,455 20.6 20.7 21.4 20.9 7.7**21.1**  
**2007**1,300,599 20.7 20.8 21.5 21 7.6**21.2**  
**2008**1,421,941 20.6 21 21.4 20.8 7.3**21.1**  
**2009**1,480,469 20.6 21 21.4 20.9 7.2**21.1**  
**2010**1,568,835 20.5 21 21.3 20.9 7.1**21**  
**2011**1,623,112 20.6 21 21.3 20.9 7.1**21.1**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1995-2010, 2011 Profile Report_
Learn Math
As you can see, ACT scores kept increasing until 2007, when there was **an all-time composite score high of 21.2.** After that, however, all subscores except English and Science consistently declined.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2012-2016
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Writing****Composite**  
**2012**1,666,017 20.5 21.1 21.3 20.9 7.1**21.1**  
**2013**1,799,243 20.2 20.9 21.1 20.7 7**20.9**  
**2014**1,845,787 20.3 20.9 21.3 20.8 7.1**21.0**  
**2015**1,924,436 20.4 20.8 21.4 20.9 6.9**21.0**  
**2016**2,090,342 20.1 20.6 21.3 20.8 19.3***20.8**
_Sources: 2012 Profile Report, 2013 Profile Report, 2014 Profile Report, 2015 Profile Report, 2016 Profile Report
*2016 Writing results are based on ACT Writing from September 2015 to August 2016, when the test was scored on a scale of 1-36._
Prep for Tests
After 2007's peak, there was **a general decline in scores across the board for nearly a decade.** In 2013, ACT, Inc. instituted changes to the ACT to better reflect national curricula, which is possibly reflected in the general stability of composites and subscores from 2013 onwards (with the exception of Math, which has steadily decreased since then).

In recent years, more and more students have been taking the ACT than ever before. But what does this change in participation rate mean for the average ACT score?
As you'll learn in this article, while ACT scores have been fairly stable in the last few years, **there have been some dips and peaks in scores in the last 30 years.** Let's take a look at what's happening.
_Feature image: Erjwiki/Wikimedia_

Let's look at some charts for average ACT scores over the past couple of decades. These will show us some trends in the ACT world that have led to recent changes in the test.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 1992-1996
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**1992-1993**875,603 20.3 20.1 21.2 20.8**20.7**  
**1994**891,714 20.3 20.2 21.2 20.9**20.8**  
**1995**945,369 20.3 20.2 21.3 21**20.8**  
**1996**924,663 20.3 20.2 21.3 21.1**20.9**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1970-1998_
In the 1992-1996 ACT scores, there was a general **increase** in Math, Reading, and Science scores.
texts.3:
## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 1997-2001
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**1997**959,301 20.3 20.6 21.3 21.1**21**  
**1998**995,039 20.4 20.8 21.4 21.1**21**  
**1999**1,019,053 20.5 20.7 21.4 21**21**  
**2000**1,065,138 20.5 20.7 21.4 21**21**  
**2001**1,069,772 20.5 20.7 21.3 21**21**
_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1970-2001_
Learn Math
In the 1997-2001 ACT scores, there was an increase in English and Math and a decline in Science and Reading. Also, in 1999, the ACT **broke the one million test-taker ceiling** for the first time.
texts.4:
## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2002-2005
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Composite**  
**2002**1,116,082 20.2 20.6 21.1 20.8**20.8**  
**2003**1,175,059 20.3 20.6 21.2 20.8**20.8**

From 2002 to 2005, there was **a slight but steady rise** in all scores across the board.
texts.5:
## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2006-2011
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Writing****Composite**  
**2006**1,206,455 20.6 20.7 21.4 20.9 7.7**21.1**  
**2007**1,300,599 20.7 20.8 21.5 21 7.6**21.2**  
**2008**1,421,941 20.6 21 21.4 20.8 7.3**21.1**

_Source: NCES Average ACT Scores 1995-2010, 2011 Profile Report_
Learn Math
As you can see, ACT scores kept increasing until 2007, when there was **an all-time composite score high of 21.2.** After that, however, all subscores except English and Science consistently declined.

## Average ACT Scores for Past Years
### Average ACT Scores 2012-2016
**Year****# of Test Takers****English****Math****Reading****Science****Writing****Composite**  
**2012**1,666,017 20.5 21.1 21.3 20.9 7.1**21.1**  
**2013**1,799,243 20.2 20.9 21.1 20.7 7**20.9**  
**2014**1,845,787 20.3 20.9 21.3 20.8 7.1**21.0**  
**2015**1,924,436 20.4 20.8 21.4 20.9 6.9**21.0**  
**2016**2,090,342 20.1 20.6 21.3 20.8 19.3***20.8**
_Sources: 2012 Profile Report, 2013 Profile Report, 2014 Profile Report, 2015 Profile Report, 2016 Profile Report
*2016 Writing results are based on ACT Writing from September 2015 to August 2016, when the test was scored on a scale of 1-36._
Prep for Tests
After 2007's peak, there was **a general decline in scores across the board for nearly a decade.** In 2013, ACT, Inc. instituted changes to the ACT to better reflect national curricula, which is possibly reflected in the general stability of composites and subscores from 2013 onwards (with the exception of Math, which has steadily decreased since then).

## ACT scores
Question:
What are the average scores for students taking the ACT?
Response:
The ACT (formerly the American College Testing Program) assessment program measures educational development and readiness to pursue college-level coursework in English, mathematics, natural science, and social studies. Student performance on the tests does not reflect innate ability and is influenced by a student's educational preparedness.
In 1995, some 38 percent of all high school graduates took the ACT.1 In 2023, some 37 percent of high school graduates were projected to take the ACT. The minimum score on the ACT is 1 and maximum score is 36.
